metaDescription: Re-indent Rust code by brace depth with 4 spaces, keeping lifetimes, raw strings and nested comments intact. No rustfmt is used.
intro: Fixes indentation, blank lines and optionally line breaks in Rust code without sending it anywhere.
why:
Messy indentation hides the structure of Rust code, and minified or copy-pasted code is worse. A re-indenter gives you the block layout back quickly.

The tool reads your code with a small scanner that knows strings, comments and raw literals, so braces inside them are ignored. It then sets the indent from bracket depth and, if you ask, puts a line break after braces and semicolons. It is not rustfmt.
howTo: Pick the indent and line break mode.
Run cargo fmt locally for the official layout.

faq.q: Is this the same as rustfmt?
faq.a: No. rustfmt also wraps lines, reorders imports and chooses a layout for chains and arguments. This tool re-indents blocks and where clauses and optionally breaks lines. Re-indenting rustfmt output with its indentation stripped restored 107 of 127 test files exactly.

faq.q: Will it change what my code does?
faq.a: It only changes whitespace outside strings, comments and raw literals. Test results: the non-whitespace text was unchanged on all test files, and re-running the tool gave the same output. Review the diff anyway.
Wrapping needs a full parser. This tool does not have one.
No. Everything runs in your browser and nothing is uploaded.
